faq.question: Is fixed or floating better for a home loan in India?
faq.answer: For most borrowers, floating. Fixed-rate home loans cost about 1 to 6 percentage points more depending on the bank, and on a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan the floating rate would have to average about 1.75 points higher for the whole term before fixed came out cheaper.

faq.question: Does a fixed home loan rate stay the same for the whole tenure?
faq.answer: Not always. Many products are fixed only for the first two to five years and then convert to floating, and some agreements allow the lender to reset the fixed rate. Check the period and any reset clause before signing.

faq.question: Can I prepay a fixed-rate home loan without charges?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. The RBI's ban on prepayment charges covers floating-rate loans to individuals. Fixed-rate loans can carry a prepayment charge if it's disclosed in the loan documents.

faq.question: Can I switch my floating home loan to a fixed rate?
faq.answer: If your lender offers it. RBI rules allow lenders to offer a switch at the time of a rate reset, and since October 2025 it's optional for them. A switching fee may apply.

faq.question: Should I fix my home loan rate before the RBI raises rates?
faq.answer: Only if the fixed rate is close to your floating rate or your budget can't take any increase. A temporary rise of even 2.5 percentage points for a few years usually costs less than paying a fixed premium for 20 years.
